news.title: Qonto Wins Banking Licence to Expand Beyond Payments for European SMBs
news.body: Qonto secured a banking licence from France’s ACPR and the European Central Bank, with initial banking offerings scheduled before November ends. Its base of more than 750,000 SMBs across eight European markets gives it an existing audience for lending and savings products that compete with incumbent business banks. The next test is the rollout: country availability, lending eligibility and deposit terms will determine how much business customers can move to Qonto.

news.title: JPMorgan Restores Processing After Software Bug Delays Payments Across Bank Boundaries
news.body: JPMorgan said a software bug in on-premise hardware systems delayed transactions on November 16 before normal processing resumed that evening. The disruption also affected counterparties sending or receiving payments involving JPMorgan, showing how a bank-level failure can delay transactions for customers elsewhere without establishing a failure of Zelle itself. Banks reviewing the incident should separate internal processing failures from network outages in customer communications and verify that delayed payments reconcile correctly.

news.title: TPG Nears Reported BILL Deal, Adding Another Potential Accounts-Payable Software Investment
news.body: TPG was reportedly nearing a take-private agreement for BILL Holdings, whose market capitalization stood at approximately $4.8 billion; negotiations remained ongoing, with no agreed price disclosed. TPG already has ownership exposure to AvidXchange following its $2.2 billion acquisition, making its interest relevant to competing accounts-payable platforms and accounting-firm partners. A definitive agreement is the next milestone; customers have no announced product combination or integration plan on which to base purchasing decisions.

news.title: KeyBank Adds Zact Expense Tools to Compete With Corporate-Card Fintechs
news.body: KeyBank launched KeyExpenseIQ with Zact, combining employee cards, real-time spending controls, receipt capture and automated expense workflows after evaluating 23 providers over two years. The partnership lets KeyBank offer commercial clients capabilities associated with Brex and Ramp while retaining its banking relationships and distribution. Customer activation, card spending and retention—not the feature list—will establish whether the product helps KeyBank retain business that might otherwise go to fintech rivals.

news.title: FIS Integration Gives Banks Access to Splitit Instalments Using Existing Credit
news.body: Splitit announced an integration with FIS Total Issuing Solutions that gives financial institutions access to instalments funded through consumers’ existing credit. That offers participating banks a route into checkout financing without requiring cardholders to establish a separate lending relationship with a third-party BNPL provider. Named issuer activations, merchant coverage and consumer terms are the next milestones; the announcement disclosed neither participating-bank counts nor launch volumes.

perspective: Qonto expands into banking and KeyBank adds expense tools, alongside JPMorgan’s processing recovery, reported accounts-payable deal talks and card-linked instalments.

curiosity.text: In 1974, France’s Carte Bleue and six other banks formed the Groupement des Cartes Bancaires to create a shared card-payment network, helping cards work across banks rather than only within the issuing bank’s own system. The network later became known as CB, a reminder that payment interoperability often starts with competitors agreeing on common rules. Source: CB, “The history of CB” — https://www.cartes-bancaires.com/en/our-history/
